His mines combined thick seams with productive equipment to lower costs. After selling control of Foresight, the American coal entrepreneur turned to developing Canadian mines, continuing a career rooted in West Virginia mining.

long_biography.plain_text:
Christopher Cline entered the coal industry through his father Paul, a contract miner in West Virginia. When his father became ill, Cline helped arrange a borrowed-money buyout of the business partner rather than a sale of the family operation. He worked long shifts underground and reinvested early business gains in further mining ventures.

Cline maintained strong links to his home state through giving. West Virginia University and Marshall University received substantial support, and Marshall named an athletic complex after him. His family foundation pledged funding for an indoor sports centre at the Raleigh County YMCA.

Canadian activity through death supports continued Energy/Founder classification, but the exact final personal asset mix is not public.
